goals: mechanistic: quantify the lag between today's surface infiltration and its arrival as recharge at the real water table, as a function of vadose-zone thickness and soil
validation: constrain the initial/steady water-table depth against observations (recharge timing itself is unvalidatable in-domain)
key_processes: surface infiltration / net drainage flux generation (ELM)
transient variably-saturated vadose-zone flow and wetting-front travel time (PFLOTRAN)
water-table depth as lower boundary controlling travel distance

model_choice.rationale: ELM forces the surface infiltration/drainage flux but collapses deep drainage to a bottom flux with a crude aquifer and no explicit vadose transit time; the timing question requires a transient unsaturated-zone model driven by ELM.
model_choice.coupling_note: One-way ELM -> PFLOTRAN: ELM surface infiltration / net recharge flux drives the top BC of a transient Richards (variably-saturated) vadose column terminating at the real WTD. The coupler AND transient unsaturated PFLOTRAN mode are both unbuilt; listed in requires_capabilities.

answerable: ELM-side surface infiltration / net drainage flux time series per column under real NLDAS forcing and SSURGO soil
initial/steady water-table depth per column via Fan-2013 WTD warm start, validatable against USGS wells
relative ordering of vadose-zone thickness across the domain (deep upland vs shallow riparian) as a travel-distance proxy

not_answerable.aspect: when today's infiltration actually arrives as recharge at the water table (the core travel-time question)
not_answerable.why: single-column ELM has no explicit multi-meter vadose transit physics; PFLOTRAN as available is steady-state groundwater, not transient unsaturated Richards; no ELM->PFLOTRAN coupler exists
not_answerable.needs: ELM->PFLOTRAN one-way coupler + transient variably-saturated PFLOTRAN vadose configuration

not_answerable.aspect: validation of recharge magnitude or timing
not_answerable.why: brief lists recharge observations as MISSING in-domain
not_answerable.needs: in-domain recharge / vadose tracer or lysimeter observations

coupling_design.driver: ELM surface infiltration / net drainage flux (QINFL / QDRAI-QRECHARGE) -> PFLOTRAN top recharge flux BC of a vertical vadose column
coupling_design.temporal_mapping: ELM daily-to-monthly flux time series (multi-year, post-spin-up) -> PFLOTRAN transient top-flux BC; optional conservative tracer pulse to read out breakthrough (first-arrival and median transit time) at the water table
coupling_design.receiving_setup: 1-D transient variably-saturated Richards column per ELM location, layered with SSURGO-derived unsaturated properties, thickness = Fan-2013 WTD, lower BC = fixed head at the water table
coupling_design.compare: coupled vadose transit time / recharge breakthrough vs ELM-standalone assumption of near-instantaneous drainage to the aquifer; standalone is expected to fail most where WTD is deep (long unsaturated column) and where low-K soils buffer the front

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (WTD-depth band x soil texture class)
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 3 WTD bands x 3 texture classes spans the two travel-time controls (distance and conductivity) with one column per cell; this is the smallest set that resolves the deep-vs-shallow x fast-vs-slow contrast the question hinges on. Light replication deferred until the coupler exists.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate contrast columns in valley bottoms/riparian corridors (shallow WTD, short transit) versus upland benches (deep WTD, long transit); the largest coupled-vs-standalone divergence is expected on deep, fine-textured columns.
sampling_strategy.replication: None in this probe design; add replicates per WTD band once the coupler is validated on one column.

sampling_plan.reason: shortest, fastest transit — near-instantaneous recharge end-member where ELM-standalone should be adequate.
short distance but low-K buffering isolates the soil control on lag at shallow water table.
central/typical Naches condition; replicated lightly as the modal case anchoring the transit-time gradient.
long distance but high K — tests whether conductivity offsets thickness.
long transit modal-soil case; expected large coupled-vs-standalone divergence.
worst-case longest lag (deep + low K) — where ELM's instantaneous-drainage assumption fails most; replicated to check robustness.

validation_design.observation_source: Fan et al. 2013 WTD prior + USGS wells
validation_design.comparison: co-located where USGS wells fall near a column, else analog against the Fan prior used for warm start; report drift of ELM 1-D equilibrium from Fan lateral-flow equilibrium as a result
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on USGS well density within the HUC

validation_design.comparison: GAP — no co-located data; can only be sanity-checked against literature vadose transit-time ranges as an analog, clearly not co-located validation

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS forcing, native SSURGO soil, Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start, multi-year run for stable drainage flux

requires_capabilities.why: map ELM surface/drainage flux time series onto PFLOTRAN top BC
available PFLOTRAN is steady-state groundwater; transit time needs transient unsaturated flow
read out first-arrival and median transit time at the water table
set each column's initial water table to real depth (aquifer clamp 0.05-28.8 m; deep uplands may pin aquifer empty)
requires_capabilities.blocks: meaningful vadose column thickness and initial state

requires_capabilities.why: recharge/drainage are slow states; cold start gives initialization artifacts
brief lists recharge observations as missing

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM + gridded WTD (Fan) + SSURGO sampler and HUC boundary resolver
requires_capabilities.why: expand stratification rules into concrete points

assumptions: Fan-2013 WTD is treated as the 'real' water-table depth and as the PFLOTRAN lower boundary; its lateral-flow equilibrium differs from ELM's 1-D equilibrium, so some drift is expected and reported.
Naches is within CONUS, so NLDAS-2 12 km forcing applies; sub-12 km terrain/precip is unresolved but not the driver here.
Soil texture classes are proxied from SSURGO; unsaturated hydraulic parameters derive from texture.
One-way (ELM->PFLOTRAN) coupling is adequate; no water-table feedback on the ELM root zone is represented.
Deep-upland columns may exceed ELM's 28.8 m aquifer range, pinning the aquifer empty — treated as a known limitation.
open_questions: How many USGS wells actually fall inside HUC 17030002, and at what depths, for co-located WTD validation?
Is any vadose tracer, lysimeter, or age-dating (e.g. tritium/CFC) data available to constrain transit time even at an analog site?
What forcing window and spin-up length does the user want (single wet/dry year vs multi-decade climatology of recharge)?
Should transit time be reported per storm event, seasonally, or as a long-term mean lag?
